. iPadOS and macOS were once two completely different software platforms, but since iPadOS 26, the two have become increasingly similar. This year, this trend is even more pronounced — iPadOS 27 adds three features that bring the iPad closer to the Mac.

#1: Status bar displays the app name

I use my M5 iPad Pro with the Magic Keyboard almost all the time. For keyboard users, the iPad has always had one problem — the lack of a clear "current app" indicator.

If only one app is on screen, it's not an issue. But when several apps are open at the same time, it's easy to hit the wrong keyboard shortcut. I can't count how many times I've thought a shortcut would trigger within one app, only for it to execute in another.

The Mac solved this problem long ago, displaying the current app's name in the top-left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 can do that too.

iPadOS 27 users will see the current app's name in the status bar, alongside other status bar information like the time and date. This isn't a huge change, but using the iPad with a keyboard is noticeably smoother.

#2: A permanently visible menu bar

Another welcome change in iPadOS 27 is the ability to set the menu bar to remain visible at all times.

Apple brought the menu bar to the iPad for the first time last year. But unlike the Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appears when the user actively summons it.

In the iPadOS 27 Settings, under "Multitasking & Gestures," there is a new option called "Auto-show and hide menu bar."

Simply turn this option off, and the menu bar will stay displayed at all times. I've already been using it this way during the iPadOS beta — it's one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Everyday operation speed closer to the Mac

Although I really love my iPad and I'm grateful for the new features iPadOS 26 and 27 bring, I still sometimes get frustrated by how slow some basic operations can be. As I wrote earlier this year: "The iPadOS right-click menu often feels slow and laggy, but on the Mac it's instant."

Fortunately, Apple has been working hard this year to narrow that gap, and I'm happy to say that iPadOS 27 does bring noticeable improvements to the speed of these everyday operations.

Apple says right-click menus open faster when using a cursor, and I can clearly feel it myself. Browsing files and transferring them to an external hard drive is "up to 5 times faster" — Apple says it's now just as fast as Finder on the Mac. Apps launch more responsively, and window management — minimising, dragging or switching windows — is much smoother.

There are still areas where the Mac is faster than the iPad, and the iPad occasionally has a little lag. But overall, the speed improvements in iPadOS 27 are a big step in the right direction.

Which new features and changes in iPadOS 27 suit you best? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
